title: Feasibility and Acceptability of the Menstrual Cup for Non-Surgical Management of Vesicovaginal Fistula
author: Gabriel Y. K. Ganyaglo
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.sjfecjn

steps.title: Identify and enroll participants
steps.instruction: Screen women attending the VVF pre‑operative clinic for eligibility, explain the study, obtain written informed consent, and assign a unique subject ID; if more eligible women are present than needed, randomize enrollment by having each woman draw a paper marked 1 (invite) or 0 (do not invite).

steps.title: Train participants on cup use
steps.instruction: Teach each participant, in her preferred local language, hand hygiene, vaginal insertion, removal techniques, and cup washing; allow ample practice time and encourage questions.

steps.title: Ensure adequate hydration
steps.instruction: Counsel participants to drink enough water to produce free‑flowing, colorless, odorless urine and confirm optimal hydration status using a urine‑color chart.

steps.title: Conduct baseline 2‑hour pad test
steps.instruction: Give each participant standardized sanitary pads to wear inside disposable underwear for a continuous two‑hour period while walking and performing usual daily activities; allow use of more than one pad if needed; after two hours, weigh each wet pad, subtract its dry weight, and record the total wet‑minus‑dry weight as the baseline urine‑leakage volume (ml).

steps.title: Insert menstrual cup and repeat pad test
steps.instruction: Instruct the participant to insert the menstrual cup, then repeat the two‑hour pad test under the same activity conditions; after two hours, weigh the wet pads, subtract dry weights, and record the leakage volume (ml) with the cup in place.

steps.title: Assess safety of vaginal mucosa
steps.instruction: After removal of the cup and pads, have a non‑study clinician examine the vaginal mucosa for erythema, edema/induration, erosion, and bleeding, and document any findings.

steps.title: Collect acceptability questionnaire
steps.instruction: Read a structured questionnaire to the participant covering demographics, perceived severity of leakage, perceived efficacy of the cup, and overall acceptability, and record the responses.

steps.title: Record feasibility metrics
steps.instruction: Throughout the study, log enrollment numbers, consent rates, and any issues with data collection to inform planning of future trials.
